_comment: Shared by BOTH renderers — the JS core imports this file at build time and the Python LIGHT renderer reads it at run time, so these values are stated once and cannot drift between the two. Colours: owner decree 2026-07-28.

axisTiers._comment: A direction's TIER is decided by how many cube letters it carries: one letter is a face normal, two an edge midpoint, three a vertex diagonal. `sacred` is not a fourth geometry — it is the one vertex diagonal a model may single out, and it is dressed and sized apart from the human three.

cellKinds._comment: A seat's kind decides which group it sits in and how big its marker is. Radii are fractions of the model size.

modelScene._comment: How a model's data becomes a scene. Fractions of the model size, so one set of numbers dresses a 1-unit cube and a 100-unit one alike.

hexagram._comment: The Hexagram X-ray overlay: the two triangles a cube's silhouette splits into when seen down a body diagonal (six equatorial face-diagonals, root Rule 19 — computed from the chosen diagonal, never per-scene coordinates). A scene may override the colours; the builder's own defaults reuse axisColors.sacred and neutral.joint rather than inventing new hues, so nothing here restates a colour that already exists above.

axisColors._comment: Owner decree 2026-07-28. Every non-primary colour is COMPUTED from the pole hues (root Rule 19) — never enumerated per axis. A two-letter direction blends its two poles and is then THINNED BY MOONLIGHT, which is what stops any edge colour from landing on a pole hue (the naive blue+yellow collision). A three-letter direction blends its three poles and is DEEPENED, so the vertex family reads heavier than the edge family. The singled-out sacred diagonal wears none of the six: white-gold, the seventh dress.
axisColors._thresholds: Guards, not knobs: `minPoleDistance` is the collision rule with teeth — no derived colour may sit this close to one of the six poles. `minSeatDistance` is the weaker promise that no two seats collapse into one colour; the closest pair is inherently the two body diagonals whose three poles are complementary and therefore average to grey (currently 17 apart), so this is set just below that.

switcher._comment: Two independent flat parameters. `register` swaps which vocabulary speaks; `reading` chooses which radial stops are lit. Both are plain names, so a timeline steps them like any other non-numeric channel.

radial._comment: The radial law: the luminous stop sits INSIDE the geometric end, the fallen stop PAST it. Factors of the arm length.

animation._comment: Playback is fixed-timestep so the same scene evaluates identically in both renderers: `fps` is the step rate AND the granularity of a single-frame step. `maxStep` caps the catch-up after a stall so a hidden tab does not fast-forward the scene.
